case_title: Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana & Anr.
accused_socioeconomic_status: Alleged only in the FIR: the accused earns about Rs. 1,50,000 a month. The Court made no finding on this.
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband and wife). A divorce petition filed by the accused in July 2019 and a domestic violence case filed by his mother were also pending between them.
evidence_type: Documentary: the FIR and chargesheet papers. No witness testimony or medical evidence is discussed in the judgment.
trial_court_outcome: Not stated. The case was pending before the Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Hisar; no decision is recorded.
high_court_outcome: Quashing petition dismissed; High Court declined to quash the criminal proceedings under s.482 Cr.P.C. (judgment dated 05.04.2022)
neutral_facts: The victim alleged that after her marriage the accused's family repeatedly demanded further dowry. She said her family had already given cash for a car, gold ornaments and furniture, and that her stridhan was handed over at the wedding. She alleged that the accused's family taunted her about inadequate dowry and beat and abused her over food, household work, and demands for gold bangles and a diamond set. She alleged that the accused beat her when he was drunk, controlled her salary and pocket money, did not allow her to make phone calls, and had an extra-marital affair she was threatened not to disclose. She further alleged that during the Covid-19 lockdown in March 2020 the accused disconnected water and television services and took their minor son away, and that she was forced to return to her parents' home. She alleged that the accused refused to return her stridhan and threatened to kill her if she complained to the police. The complaint was lodged in April 2021 and gave no specific dates or times for the alleged incidents. Police investigated and filed a chargesheet only against the accused. Proceedings against the four other named family members were dropped. The evidence before the court consists of the complaint and the chargesheet papers. No witness testimony or medical evidence is discussed.
offence_severity: Maximum three years' imprisonment and fine (s.498A IPC, as quoted in the judgment from Preeti Gupta). No minimum is stated.
physical_harm: Alleged in the FIR only: repeated beatings and abuse. The judgment records no injuries and makes no finding.
financial_property_loss: Alleged only: stridhan (jewellery) not returned and the victim's salary taken by the accused's family. No value is stated.
premeditation_planning: Not stated. The Court made no finding on premeditation.
motive: Court's finding: the FIR was a counterblast to the divorce petition and domestic violence case, filed to harass the accused and his family. Alleged: dowry demand.
key_evidence_accepted: The FIR and chargesheet papers, which the Court found vague, general and without specific dates; the unexplained delay of about two years after the divorce petition.
witness_credibility: Not stated. No witness credibility assessment is made. The Court noted that police dropped the proceedings against the other four accused.
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 05.04.2022; Supreme Court: 03 May 2024
legal_representation: Appellant: Yusuf, Advocate. State (Respondent No. 1): Chritarth Palli, with Dr. Monika Gusain, Parveen Kumar Aggarwal, Abhishek Grover, Vivek Gupta and Vikas Gupta for the respondents.
investigation_status: FIR No. 95 of 2021 registered on 09.04.2021; chargesheet filed 13.10.2021 against the accused only; closure report filed for the other four accused
appeal_history: Trial court: no decision; the case was pending before the Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Hisar. High Court: quashing petition dismissed on 05.04.2022. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court order set aside and proceedings quashed.
prosecution_argument: State: the investigation was fair, and the investigating officer thought fit to charge the accused given the nature of the allegations. Complainant: dowry demands, beatings, withholding of salary, and an affair; the domestic violence case was frivolous.
defence_argument: The FIR was a counterblast to the divorce petition and domestic violence case, filed after an unexplained delay of over 11 months. The allegations were vague and general, with no specific incident of harassment.
legal_principle_applied: Inherent power under s.482 Cr.P.C.: quashing to prevent abuse of process and secure the ends of justice. Vague, general and sweeping allegations in a matrimonial dispute are an abuse of process. The power also extends after chargesheet is filed.
precedent_relied_upon: R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866; State of A.P. v. Vangaveeti Nagaiah, (2009) 12 SCC 466; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand, 2010 Cri LJ 4303; Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014); Geeta Mehrotra v. State of U.P., (2012) 10 SCC 741; B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC 675; Mahmood Ali v. State of U.P., 2023 SCC OnLine SC 950
other_sentence_order: Request to the Legislature to reconsider ss.85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 before they come into force. Registry directed to send copies of the judgment to the Union Law Secretary and Union Home Secretary (para 44, page 35).
